themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints have spiked 967% this week with 4 complaints versus a historical average of 0.4 per week, suggesting either a sudden removal incident, coordinated theft, or weather damage affecting directional and regulatory signage across the district.
evidence: 4 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.49)
967% spike in a single-week period indicates acute rather than chronic issue
High z-score (7.49) confirms statistical significance and not random variation
reporting_angles: Ground truth: Visit multiple locations to photograph and map which signs are missing and what types (stop signs, street names, parking regulation signs)
Interview DOT about any reported removals, maintenance work, or theft reports in the district this week
Community safety angle: Do missing signs pose traffic or navigation hazards?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints have jumped 223% this week to 25 complaints versus an 8-week average of 7.8 per week, representing a substantial and acute degradation of road quality potentially triggered by recent weather or deferred maintenance.
evidence: 25 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (223% increase)
Z-score of 4.54 indicates highly significant statistical spike
Timing suggests correlation with winter weather or recent storm damage
reporting_angles: Document street conditions: identify and photograph worst-affected blocks and intersection types (potholes, cracking, flooding vulnerability)
Interview residents and delivery workers on accessibility and safety impacts, especially for elderly, disabled, or families with strollers
Contact DDOT and NYC Parks on repair backlog, budget constraints, or weather response delays

themes_detail.label: Animals in Parks Spiking
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints have surged 433% this week with 6 reports versus a baseline of 1.1 per week, possibly indicating coyote, raccoon, or rat activity driven by seasonal migration or inadequate waste management around Coney Island's park spaces.
evidence: 6 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 6.24)
Timing aligns with winter season when wildlife often enters urban areas seeking food
Parks mentioned include Seaside Park and adjacent green spaces (active ULURP project: Seaside Park & Community Arts Center special permit)
reporting_angles: Identify which species are being reported (coyotes, raccoons, foxes, rats) and speak with residents who filed complaints about sightings
Interview NYC Parks & Recreation about wildlife management protocols, trash containment, and whether they've issued warnings
Public health angle: any reported bites or attacks; disease vector concerns (rabies, mange)

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Complaints Triple
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos-related complaints have spiked 1100% last week with 3 reports versus a historical average of 0.2 per week, suggesting potential building code violations or discovery of hazardous materials in older structures undergoing renovation in the district.
evidence: 3 asbestos complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
222 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days with 166 alteration permits—likely renovation work exposing asbestos in pre-1980s buildings
Coney Island/Brighton Beach has many older residential and commercial buildings with legacy asbestos insulation
reporting_angles: Investigate which properties filed the asbestos complaints: cross-reference with DOB permits to identify problem buildings
Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection and asbestos remediation contractors about enforcement and removal standards
Resident health impact: speak with tenants in buildings where asbestos was discovered about evacuation protocols and indoor air quality concerns
Regulatory compliance angle: are contractors properly licensed for asbestos abatement?

themes_detail.label: Dumpster and Waste Management Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints have increased 1100% last week with 3 reports versus a baseline of 0.2 per week, paired with a concurrent 700% spike in street-sweeping complaints (8 reports vs. 1.0 average), indicating systemic sanitation breakdown affecting waste collection and street cleanliness.
evidence: 3 dumpster complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
8 street-sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.29)
Combined spike suggests either contractor service failure, resource shortage, or operational change affecting waste removal across the district
reporting_angles: Document ground conditions: identify overflowing dumpsters, unswept streets, and rodent or pest activity associated with waste accumulation
Interview DSNY about staffing levels, contract management, and service frequency for this district
Resident quality-of-life impact: how have beaches, parks, and residential blocks been affected by unsanitary conditions?
Check if DSNY has issued any service notices or temporary suspensions in CD 313
